statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-42258 (GHSA-75xq-5h9v-w6px): before net-imap 0.4.24, 0.5.14 and 0.6.4, Net::IMAP sends Symbol arguments (IMAP system flags) to the server without validation, so a Symbol containing a space or CRLF can end the current command and inject new IMAP commands: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-75xq-5h9v-w6px. On the 0.4 release line it is fixed in net-imap 0.4.24, whose release notes name this advisory (https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.4.24), by https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/commit/bbd9eb7ecca506fa43b656368f7aebef8ac09182 (Strictly validate symbol flag arguments), which makes lib/net/imap/command_data.rb validate every Symbol argument as a flag before it is sent. The DHI ruby-3.3 package for Alpine 3.23 is published as 3.3.10-r0, 3.3.10-r1, 3.3.11-r1, 3.3.11-r2, 3.3.11-r3, 3.3.12-r3, 3.3.13-r3, 3.3.14-r3 and 3.3.14-r4 on x86_64 and aarch64 (ruby-3.3-libs and ruby-3.3-full 3.3.11-r1 are published for aarch64 only), as listed in the repository index on 2026-11-27. net-imap is not in the ruby-3.3 package itself: it is installed by the ruby3.3-net-imap gem package, built from the same source but carrying the gem's version, which ruby-3.3-full depends on. The range below is written in the ruby-3.3 package's own versions, so each ruby-3.3 build is placed by the net-imap release its build installs. We downloaded every published ruby3.3-net-imap package (0.4.21-r0, 0.4.21-r1, 0.4.21-r2, 0.4.21-r3, 0.4.25-r3 and 0.4.25-r4) and every published ruby-3.3-libs package for both architectures, each checked against its repository index checksum, and compared each installed net-imap lib directory with the release from rubygems.org: 0.4.21-r0 to 0.4.21-r2 are identical to net-imap 0.4.21, 0.4.21-r3 (despite its label) is identical to net-imap 0.4.24, and 0.4.25-r3 and 0.4.25-r4 are identical to net-imap 0.4.25. The repository index records the same build commit for ruby3.3-net-imap 0.4.21-r3 and ruby-3.3 3.3.11-r3, so 3.3.11-r3 is the build that replaced Ruby 3.3.11's bundled net-imap 0.4.21 with 0.4.24. Ruby 3.3.10 and 3.3.11 bundle net-imap 0.4.21 and Ruby 3.3.12, 3.3.13 and 3.3.14 bundle 0.4.25 (https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/v3_3_11/gems/bundled_gems, https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/v3_3_12/gems/bundled_gems), so 3.3.10-r0 to 3.3.11-r2 ship net-imap 0.4.21, 3.3.11-r3 ships 0.4.24, and 3.3.12-r3 onward ship 0.4.25. No ruby-3.3-libs build installs net-imap; ruby-3.3-libs 3.3.11-r3 only carries a cached copy of the net-imap 0.4.24 gem archive (usr/lib/ruby/gems/3.3.0/cache/net-imap-0.4.24.gem, identical to the rubygems.org file), which Ruby does not load. The installed lib/net/imap/command_data.rb validates Symbol arguments (Flag.validate) in the 0.4.24 and 0.4.25 copies and not in the 0.4.21 copies. Both architectures agree for every build. So every ruby-3.3 build before 3.3.11-r3 ships net-imap without this fix, and 3.3.11-r3 and every later build ship it: the range is fixed at 3.3.11-r3.

CVE-2026-42258 (GHSA-75xq-5h9v-w6px): before net-imap 0.4.24, 0.5.14 and 0.6.4, Symbol arguments, which Net::IMAP sends as IMAP system flags, are written to the socket without validation, so a Symbol built from caller-supplied input can contain spaces or CRLF and inject further IMAP commands: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-75xq-5h9v-w6px. On the 0.5 release line it is fixed in net-imap 0.5.14, whose release notes name this advisory: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.5.14. In the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, net-imap ships in the ruby3.4-net-imap package, which is built from the ruby-3.4 source with its own version number; ruby-3.4-full depends on it. We downloaded every published ruby3.4-net-imap package for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64, checked each against its repository index checksum, and compared its installed lib directory with the net-imap release from rubygems.org; each matches its release byte for byte: 0.5.8-r0 and 0.5.8-r1 install net-imap 0.5.8, 0.5.8-r2 installs net-imap 0.5.14, and 0.5.15-r2, 0.5.15-r3 and 0.5.15-r4 install net-imap 0.5.15. Each ruby-3.4 build is built together with the ruby3.4-net-imap package of the same package release (-rN): 3.4.8-r0 to 3.4.9-r1 with net-imap 0.5.8 (ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.8-r0 and 0.5.8-r1); 3.4.9-r2, which upgrades the bundled net-imap to 0.5.14, with ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.8-r2; and 3.4.10-r2 and every later build, whose Ruby releases bundle net-imap 0.5.15, with ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.15-r2 to 0.5.15-r4 (0.5.15-r2 was published with ruby-3.4 3.4.10-r2). The published DHI Ruby 3.4.9 and 3.4.10 dev images for Alpine 3.23 install ruby-3.4 3.4.9-r2 with ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.8-r2 (net-imap 0.5.14) and ruby-3.4 3.4.10-r3 with ruby3.4-net-imap 0.5.15-r3 (net-imap 0.5.15), on amd64 and arm64. The ruby-3.4-libs 3.4.9-r2 package also carries the net-imap 0.5.14 gem archive, identical to the rubygems.org file; ruby-3.4-libs 3.4.9-r1 carries none. So the first published ruby-3.4 build that ships the fix is 3.4.9-r2: the builds before it ship net-imap 0.5.8, and it and every later build ship net-imap 0.5.14 or 0.5.15.

CVE-2026-42258 (GHSA-75xq-5h9v-w6px): in the Ruby net-imap gem, Net::IMAP sends Symbol arguments to the server without validating them, so an application that builds a Symbol from untrusted input can be made to send additional IMAP commands (command injection): https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-75xq-5h9v-w6px. Upstream fixed it in net-imap 0.4.24 on the 0.4 line, 0.5.14 on the 0.5 line and 0.6.4 on the 0.6 line; the 0.6.4 release notes list GHSA-75xq-5h9v-w6px: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.6.4. The DHI ruby-4.0 package for Alpine 3.23 is published as 4.0.1-r0, 4.0.1-r1, 4.0.2-r1, 4.0.2-r2, 4.0.3-r2, 4.0.4-r2, 4.0.4-r3, 4.0.5-r3, 4.0.6-r3, 4.0.6-r4, 4.0.7-r4, 4.0.9-r4, 4.0.10-r4 and 4.0.10-r5, for x86_64 and aarch64. It ships net-imap in its ruby4.0-net-imap gem package, which carries the gem's version rather than Ruby's, so the range below is written in the ruby-4.0 package's own versions, and each ruby-4.0 build is placed by the net-imap its ruby4.0-net-imap package installs. The gem package keeps the gem's own version but takes its -rN release number from the Ruby build that produced it, and the repository keeps one copy of each package version, so the gem package versions published under a given -rN are exactly the net-imap releases the Ruby builds with that -rN shipped. We read Net::IMAP::VERSION in lib/net/imap.rb of every published ruby4.0-net-imap package for both architectures, each verified against the repository index checksum, and listed the contents of every published ruby-4.0-libs package: the published ruby4.0-net-imap packages are 0.6.2-r0, 0.6.2-r1, 0.6.2-r2, 0.6.2-r3, 0.6.4.1-r3, 0.6.4.1-r4 and 0.6.4.1-r5. 0.6.2-r0, -r1 and -r2 install net-imap 0.6.2, the only gem version under -r0, -r1 and -r2, so 4.0.1-r0 through 4.0.4-r2 ship 0.6.2. Under -r3 two gem versions exist: 0.6.2-r3, which despite its label installs net-imap 0.6.4, and 0.6.4.1-r3, which installs net-imap 0.6.4.1. The 4.0.4-r3 and 4.0.5-r3 builds are the ones that replaced their bundled net-imap with 0.6.4: ruby-4.0-libs 4.0.4-r3 and 4.0.5-r3 both carry the net-imap-0.6.4 gem archive that install left behind, while no other ruby-4.0-libs build carries a net-imap archive; 4.0.6-r3 ships 0.6.4.1. 0.6.4.1-r4 and 0.6.4.1-r5 install net-imap 0.6.4.1, so 4.0.6-r4, 4.0.7-r4, 4.0.9-r4, 4.0.10-r4 and 4.0.10-r5 ship 0.6.4.1. Both architectures agree for every build. Every ruby-4.0 build before 4.0.4-r3 ships a net-imap without this fix, and 4.0.4-r3 is the first that ships net-imap 0.6.4, so the range is introduced at the first published build and fixed at 4.0.4-r3.
